summary: Postinstall dropper installs XMRig cryptominer with stealth persistence
details: The package's `postinstall` hook runs `scripts/miner.sh`, which fetches a gzip-compressed payload from amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com (using a hardcoded AWS access key <redacted> in a presigned URL), writes it to `/tmp/.smi`, and executes it via `sh` on every `npm install`. If root or passwordless sudo is available, the script runs `sh /tmp/.smi agent` to install a persistent agent (cron/relay/tor per in-script comments). Otherwise, it extracts an embedded XMRig binary (base64/tar.gz blob after a `__PAYLOAD__` marker), writes a Monero pool configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` pointing at networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443 with wallet 49u1mKb1dNoMixgRHt11Ra32D1w4hviUuRDbaJhXFwXUjQP4FiHsSjnDa7XZepDUW1Tx6HhR6gFwWgbuwNxby4UAMiqxieX, copies the miner to `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/<stealth-name>` using a system-daemon-like name pool (`edid-mon`, `smmon`, `irqstatsd`,...), and backgrounds it with `nohup`. Installing the package results in unconditional remote code execution on the installer's host, cryptomining compute/electricity theft, and persistence that is non-trivial to detect and remove.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
